title: Special Report on Climate Change and Land — soil carbon and land degradation
claim: Land degradation and declining soil organic carbon reduce the resilience of agricultural soils to rainfall variability and rising temperatures, while restorative land management practices can help rebuild that resilience.
evidence_text: The IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Land links declining soil organic carbon to reduced water-holding capacity and structural stability, compounding the impact of rising temperatures and more variable rainfall on agricultural productivity and ecosystem function. The report identifies restorative practices — including reduced tillage, cover cropping, and agroforestry — as measures that can rebuild soil carbon and associated climate resilience over time.
